newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Systemat asks listing of 708,480 shares.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Systemat asks listing of 708,480 shares.

text.p: Belgian independent computer services provider Systemat said it requested on Monday the listing of 708,480 ordinary shares on the Brussels primary market's double fixing segment.
It said the operation consisted of a capital increase by issuing new shares offered at the listing, and a public offer for the sale of existing shares.
In total the offer represented 49 percent of the capital.
Systemat, founded in 1981, said it expected the bourse listing, organised by Banque Bruxelles Lambert (BBL), to take place before the end of March.
It said that accelerated growth since 1994, favourable prospects for coming years and the important new funds it had to put in justified the decision of the company to be listed.
Systemat said its 1996 consolidated net profit jumped to 76.2 million francs from 11.5 million in 1995. Turnover rose to 3.42 billion francs from 1.88 billion in 1995.
